headline: CRA-Meldepflichten gelten bereits; CBAM-Regeln für Drittlandspreise und Gratiszertifikate werden konkreter

summary.text: An industry joint position flags unresolved overlaps between the Cyber Resilience Act and the Machinery Regulation, so manufacturers may face double compliance work.

CRA vulnerability reporting duties have applied since September 2026 and full obligations follow in December 2027, so makers of connected products need a security checklist now; exida offers software for automatic risk reports.
New CBAM rules on crediting third-country carbon prices could lower costs for steel and aluminium importers, and Upper Austrian installations get free allowances for longer.
A reported exemption of UK imports from CBAM is unconfirmed, so importers should wait for the official text before changing their reporting scope.
MVTec Halcon now runs on Bosch Rexroth's ctrlX OS, and AI optical inspection and Nord's modular IIoT condition monitoring give mid-sized plants low-barrier pilots.

actions.text: Machine builders and makers of connected products: check which products fall under both the CRA and the Machinery Regulation, and start a CRA security and vulnerability-reporting checklist.

Purchasing and customs teams: check whether your steel and aluminium suppliers qualify for third-country carbon price crediting, and verify allocations. Do not act on the UK exemption until it is official.
Quality and engineering heads: scope a pilot for AI optical inspection, for example Halcon on ctrlX OS if you already use Bosch Rexroth.
